raw_text:
Below is a structured 12‑week plan integrating training, nutrition, and recovery to target fat loss, improve glycaemic control, and support overall cardiometabolic health. It’s written for a client with type 2 diabetes (on metformin) and full gym access. Build in communication with her primary care provider as needed, especially if medications change or hypoglycaemia risk increases.

Key safety notes for T2D
- Monitor blood glucose (BG): check pre-workout, occasionally mid-session for longer/harder sessions, and 1–2 hours post-workout. Aim pre-exercise BG 90–250 mg/dL (5–13.9 mmol/L). If <90, take 15–20 g fast-acting carbs and recheck; if >250 with symptoms/ketones, postpone and follow medical advice.
- Metformin alone has low hypoglycaemia risk, but combined with exercise and calorie deficit, she may still dip—carry glucose tabs or juice.
- Hydration: at least 2–2.5 L/day; more if sweating.
- Foot care: proper footwear; inspect feet daily.
- Progress gradually; prioritize consistency.

Program overview
- Frequency: 5 days/week (3 resistance, 2 cardio + optional low-intensity activity). ~60–75 min sessions.
- Periodization:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and insulin sensitivity focus
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload and conditioning
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification and metabolic finisher focus
- Objective metrics: weekly scale weight, waist circumference every 2 weeks, resting BP/HR weekly, CGM or glucometer trends, RPE logs, step count (goal 7–10k/day by Week 4).

Nutrition framework (diabetes-appropriate, fat-loss oriented)
- Calorie target: start at ~25% deficit from estimated TDEE.
  - Quick estimate: For a typical 45-year-old female, 70–80 kg, moderate activity, TDEE ~1900–2200 kcal. Start 1400–1650 kcal/day, adjust based on progress (0.5–0.9% body weight loss per week). If lighter/heavier, scale accordingly.
- Macronutrients:
  - Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight/day (supports satiety and lean mass; split over 3–4 meals).
  - Fat: 25–35% of total kcal, emphasize mono-/poly-unsaturated fats.
  - Carbohydrate: remainder of calories; start at 35–45% of total kcal, distributed evenly across meals and around workouts to minimize glycaemic excursions.
- Carbohydrate quality and distribution:
  - Choose low–moderate GI, high-fiber carbs (oats, quinoa, legumes, berries, apples, non-starchy veg, sweet potato with skin, wholegrain breads/pasta).
  - Aim 25–35 g fiber/day.
  - Distribute carbs: 3 main meals with 30–45 g net carbs each; optional 1–2 snacks with 10–20 g carbs; include protein and some fat to blunt postprandial spikes.
  - Time 20–40 g carbs pre-workout if training >45 min; include 20–35 g protein post-workout with 20–40 g carbs.
- Glycaemic control tactics:
  - “Veg-first” meal sequencing: start meals with non-starchy veg/salad, then protein/fat, then carbs.
  - Add vinegar or lemon to carb-containing meals if tolerated.
  - Walk 10–15 minutes after meals, especially higher-carb meals.
- Meal composition template (examples):
  - Breakfast (30–40 g carbs): Greek yogurt (200 g) + chia (1 tbsp) + berries (1 cup) + 10–15 g nuts.
  - Lunch (35–45 g carbs): Grilled chicken salad with olive oil; ¾ cup cooked quinoa; mixed veg.
  - Dinner (30–45 g carbs): Baked salmon, roasted non-starchy veg, ½–1 cup roasted sweet potato.
  - Snacks (10–20 g carbs): Cottage cheese + cucumber; hummus + carrots; protein shake + small apple.
- Hydration/electrolytes: water as base; consider unsweetened tea/coffee; add pinch of salt to a glass of water before longer/hot workouts if needed.
- Supplements (optional, evidence-based; confirm with physician):
  - Vitamin D if deficient; omega‑3 (1–2 g EPA/DHA) if dietary intake low.
  - Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day (safe in T2D with normal renal function; monitor if renal issues).
  - Whey or casein to help meet protein goals.
  - Avoid cinnamon/berberine without physician input given metformin use.

Weekly structure (typical)
- Mon: Resistance A (Lower emphasis) + short cardio
- Tue: Cardio (Zone 2 aerobic) + core/mobility
- Wed: Resistance B (Upper emphasis)
- Thu: Active recovery (walk 30–45 min) or rest
- Fri: Resistance C (Full body/metabolic) + intervals (Phase-dependent)
- Sat: Cardio (Zone 2 or intervals per phase)
- Sun: Rest, mobility, light walk

Warm-up protocol (all sessions)
- 5–8 min easy cardio
- Dynamic mobility (hips, T‑spine, shoulders, ankles) 5 min
- 1–2 ramp-up sets for first two lifts
- Cue nasal breathing to keep early session HR controlled

Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: learn movement patterns, improve insulin sensitivity, establish consistency, accumulate steps. RPE 6–7 most work sets. Rest 60–90 s compounds, 45–60 s accessories.

Week 1
- Resistance A (Lower)
  - Goblet squat 3×10–12
  - Romanian deadlift (DB/BB) 3×10
  - Split squat (bodyweight or light DB) 3×8/side
  - Leg curl (machine) 3×12
  - Glute bridge 3×12–15
  - Finisher: Bike 8 min easy-moderate
- Cardio (Tue): Treadmill incline walk or cycle 35–40 min, Zone 2 (RPE 5–6)
- Resistance B (Upper)
  - Lat pulldown 3×10–12
  - DB bench press 3×10
  - Seated cable row 3×10–12
  - DB overhead press 3×8–10
  - Incline push-up or machine press 2×10–12
  - Cable face pull 3×12–15
  - Pallof press 3×10/side
- Resistance C (Full body, lighter)
  - Trap bar deadlift or kettlebell deadlift 3×6–8 (light-moderate)
  - Step-up 3×8/side
  - Assisted pull-up or pulldown 3×8–10
  - Push-up (incline) 3×8–10
  - Farmer carry 4×30–40 m
  - Finisher: Row 6–8 min easy-moderate
- Cardio (Sat): Zone 2 35–45 min (bike, elliptical, or brisk walk)
- Daily steps: 6–8k; post-meal walks 10–15 min after 1–2 meals.
- Nutrition: start targets; log meals 5–6 days; confirm BG responses to breakfast and dinner compositions.

Week 2
- Progress each lift by 2–5% load or +1 rep per set.
- Add core to Lower day: Side plank 3×20–30 s/side.
- Cardio: Zone 2 40–45 min Tue/Sat.
- Finisher on Fri: 5×1 min moderate cycling, 1 min easy (not all-out).
- Nutrition: Keep carbs 35–45% kcal; ensure at least 30 g protein at breakfast. Trial vinegar (1–2 tsp) before higher-carb meals.

Week 3
- Resistance: same exercises; use 3×10–12 rep ranges aiming top-end before increasing load; RPE 7.
- Introduce gentle intervals Sat: 6×45 s brisk/1:15 easy walk.
- Add mobility block Thu (15–20 min).
- Nutrition: Evaluate weekly average weight/BG. If weight loss <0.3% BW/week, reduce 100–150 kcal/day or increase steps to 8–10k.

Week 4
- Slight deload on volume (reduce 1 set on main lifts) but maintain intensity.
- Cardio: Zone 2 45–50 min once; intervals once (as Week 3).
- Nutrition: Reassess calories. Check fiber averaging 28–35 g/day; adjust vegetables/legumes as needed.

Phase 2: Progressive overload and conditioning (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: increase strength/work capacity, add structured intervals, continue steady fat loss. RPE 7–8; rest 90 s compounds, 60 s accessories.

Week 5
- Resistance A (Lower)
  - Back squat or hack squat 4×6–8
  - Romanian deadlift 4×8
  - Walking lunge 3×8/side
  - Leg press 3×10–12
  - Calf raise 3×12–15
  - Core: Hanging or captain’s chair knee raise 3×10–12
- Cardio Tue: Zone 2 45–50 min
- Resistance B (Upper)
  - Bench press (BB/DB) 4×6–8
  - One-arm DB row 4×8/side
  - Lat pulldown (wide/neutral) 3×8–10
  - Seated DB shoulder press 3×8–10
  - Cable chest-supported rear-delt fly 3×12–15
  - Cable curl 2×12, Rope pressdown 2×12
- Resistance C (Full body + metabolic)
  - Trap bar deadlift 4×5–6 (moderate)
  - Hip thrust 3×8–10
  - Push-up or machine press 3×10
  - Chest-supported row 3×10
  - Suitcase carry 4×30 m/side
  - Finisher: Bike 6×45 s hard (RPE 8) / 75 s easy
- Cardio Sat: Zone 2 45–55 min or outdoor brisk walk.
- Nutrition: If weight loss plateau, adjust to next 100–150 kcal deficit or add 10 min to two cardio sessions. Maintain carb distribution; prioritize carbs pre/post training days.

Week 6
- Progress loads by 2–5% or +1 rep on first two sets.
- Intervals Fri finisher: 7×45 s hard/75 s easy.
- Sat option: low-impact intervals 8×30 s hard/60 s easy on elliptical if joints prefer.
- Nutrition: Include 2 legume-based meals this week (e.g., lentil salad, bean chili) for fiber and satiety; monitor BG response.

Week 7
- Resistance A/B/C: keep set schemes; rotate variations to manage joints:
  - Front squat or goblet squat heavy 4×6–8 if back-squat uncomfortable.
  - Swap RDL for cable pull-throughs 4×10 if needed.
- Add loaded carries volume: 5–6 total carries/session.
- Intervals Fri: 6×60 s hard/90 s easy.
- Cardio Tue: 50–55 min Zone 2.
- Nutrition: Refeed strategy not required; instead, one higher-carb training day (increase carbs by 30–50 g from fruit/whole grains, hold fats lower) if energy is lagging; keep weekly average calories consistent.

Week 8
- Slight deload on lower-body axial load: reduce 1 set on squats/deads; keep accessories.
- Maintain cardio volumes; intervals as Week 7 or drop 1 rep if fatigue high.
- Nutrition: Reassess macros against progress and hunger. Ensure minimum protein 1.6 g/kg; if satiety low, add 5–10 g fiber/day via veggies/psyllium (start low, increase water).

Phase 3: Intensification and metabolic finishers (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: consolidate strength, increase caloric expenditure, sharpen insulin sensitivity. RPE 7–9 on main lifts; careful BG checks around harder sessions.

Week 9
- Resistance A (Lower strength + conditioning)
  - Back or front squat 5×5 (RPE 7–8)
  - RDL 4×6–8
  - Reverse lunge 3×8/side
  - Leg curl 3×10–12
  - Core: Dead bug 3×10/side
  - Finisher: Sled push/pull 6×30 m (moderate-hard, 60–90 s rest)
- Cardio Tue: Zone 2 50–60 min
- Resistance B (Upper strength)
  - Bench press 5×5
  - Chest-supported row 4×8
  - Pull-down or assisted pull-up 3×8–10
  - DB overhead press 3×8
  - Face pull 3×12–15
  - Finisher: Assault bike 5×60 s hard / 90 s easy
- Resistance C (Full body circuit, controlled)
  - Circuit x 3–4 rounds, 60 s between rounds:
    - Kettlebell deadlift 10
    - DB incline press 10
    - Seated row 10
    - Goblet squat 12
    - Plank 30–45 s
- Cardio Sat: Option A Zone 2 50–60 min; or Option B Tempo: 3×8 min at upper Zone 2/low Zone 3 with 3 min easy between.
- Nutrition: Maintain deficit; time 25–35 g carbs + 20–30 g protein 60–90 min pre-workout; same post-workout. Emphasize sodium/potassium (leafy greens, tomatoes, yogurt) to support performance.

Week 10
- Progress 5×5 loads by 2–2.5%.
- Finishers: increase sled rounds to 7; bike to 6 intervals.
- Add anti-rotational core (Pallof press 3×12/side) on Upper day.
- Nutrition: Evaluate CGM/glucose logs for post-meal spikes >180 mg/dL; if frequent, move 10–15 g carbs from breakfast to post-workout or dinner, add 5–10 g fat/protein at breakfast, and add a 10-min post-meal walk.

Week 11
- Transition to 4×4 on squat/bench with slightly higher load (RPE 8–8.5).
- Full body circuit: 4 rounds, add light battle rope 20–30 s at end of each round.
- Cardio Tue: 40 min Zone 2 + 10 min brisk walk immediately after dinner.
- Nutrition: If nearing goal or hunger high, introduce “protein-priority” day once this week (keep calories; shift carbs −25 g, fats +10 g, protein +20–25 g) on a rest/Zone 2 day.

Week 12
- Taper volume 20–30% to consolidate and reduce fatigue; keep intensity moderate (RPE 7–8).
- Reduce finishers volume by 25–30%.
- Maintain Zone 2 twice for 40–50 min.
- Reassess metrics mid- and end-week; prepare next-phase plan.
- Nutrition: Hold steady; avoid large deficits this week to support recovery. Schedule labs in coordination with her physician if due (HbA1c reassessment typically at 3 months).

Exercise details and progression cues
- Tempo: prioritize controlled eccentrics (2–3 s down) and strong intent on concentric.
- Technique first: pain-free ROM; swap exercises if any joint discomfort persists.
- Progression hierarchy: hit top of rep range at target RPE → add load 2–5% next session; if fatigued, add reps before load.
- RPE guidance: if BG trending <100 pre-session, keep RPE ≤7 and have 10–15 g carbs available.

Cardio intensity guidance
- Zone 2: conversational pace, 60–70% HRmax (approx 180 − age ± 5 rule ⇒ ~130–140 bpm as starting guide, then refine by talk test).
- Intervals: hard segments RPE 8–9 but not all-out; avoid if unwell or if BG is very high/very low.

Recovery, sleep, and stress
- Sleep: 7–9 hours; consistent schedule; cool, dark room.
- Stress: 5–10 min/day of breathing, meditation, or gentle yoga; stress spikes can elevate BG.
- Mobility: 10–15 min 2–3×/week focusing hips/thoracic spine/ankles/shoulders.
- Deloads integrated Weeks 4 and 8; adjust more if HRV/subjective fatigue flags.

Sample day (training day ~1550 kcal; adjust to body size)
- Breakfast: Veg omelet (2 whole eggs + 150 g egg whites), sautéed spinach/peppers, 1 slice high-fiber wholegrain toast, ½ avocado. (~35 g carbs, 40 g protein, 20 g fat)
- Pre-workout snack (60–90 min prior): Skyr yogurt + small banana, cinnamon. (~35 g carbs, 18 g protein)
- Post-workout/lunch: Grilled salmon bowl: salmon 140 g, quinoa ¾ cup cooked, mixed greens, olive oil/lemon dressing. (~40 g carbs, 35–40 g protein, 18 g fat)
- Snack: Cottage cheese 150 g + cucumber + 10 almonds. (~10 g carbs, 20 g protein, 8 g fat)
- Dinner: Turkey chili (beans + veg), side salad. (~30–35 g carbs, 35 g protein, 12 g fat)

Contingencies and adjustments
- Hypoglycaemia symptoms (shaky, sweaty, confused): stop activity, take 15–20 g fast-acting carbs, recheck in 15 min; repeat if needed; follow up with a balanced snack.
- High BG >250 mg/dL with symptoms: postpone intense exercise; hydrate; follow medical guidance.
- Plateaus: if weight stable 2+ weeks and adherence solid, reduce 100–150 kcal/day (primarily from carbs/fats evenly) or add 15–20 min Zone 2/week.
- Menstrual cycle/perimenopause considerations: expect potential transient water retention and BG variability; prioritize sleep and hydration; avoid overcorrecting calories during short-term fluctuations.

Outcome expectations
- Target fat loss: ~0.5–0.9% body weight/week.
- Improved fasting BG and postprandial responses within weeks; HbA1c changes measurable by ~12 weeks.
- Strength gains across major lifts; improved aerobic capacity and recovery.

Use this as a live document with weekly check-ins, BG/weight/satiety data, and joint comfort guiding micro-adjustments.
